subject: Pilot scope and legal path for ephemeral data handling (short retention pilot)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
To: Ava Hart <ava.hart@medisafe.io>, privacy@medisafe.io
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-08-03T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot scope and legal path for ephemeral data handling (short retention pilot)

Thanks again for your time earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum and make this pilot legal-ready: 

Call summary (high level)
- Goal: validate a short-retention / ephemeral path for Medisafe's conversational routing to reduce PII persistence while we evaluate integration reliability.
- Technical ask: ability to run a pilot where identifiable user PII is never written to long-term logs ( 0-retention for PII recognized), and session-level KV/cache can be configured to a short TTL.
- Legal/Compliance asks you raised: evidence of deletion, key management (CMK/HSM), residency (US-only), and audit logs/audit evidence for the pilot.

Proposed pilot scope (option A — narrow):
- Demo environment in us-east-1 with customer-facing model endpoints.
- KV cache retention: 24 hours (configurable) for the pilot; option to evaluate 0-retention for PII fields through on-the-fly scrubbing.
- Persistent logs: minimal request/response traces only (token-level redaction).
- Access controls: role-based access + strict ACL for logs; audit logging enabled.

What we can provide now (attachments):
- Redwood-DataRetention-FAQ.pdf (attached) — outlines retention knobs and evidence types.
- Proposed SOW language snippet and pilot checklist (I can send a draft after we agree scope).

Open items / asks for Medisafe
1) Can you share a short privacy/PII matrix or list of fields that must be treated as non-persistent? (we referenced this on the call)
2) Confirm whether customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) are required for the pilot or only for production.
3) Any internal legal/infosec folks you'd like included in the follow-up — we should loop them in before the SOW draft.

Next steps (proposed)
- Ava: send PII matrix + confirm KMS requirement (by Aug 5).
- Redwood (Ben/Tessa): share SOW draft + option matrix (24h vs 7d vs 0-retention alternatives) and list of evidence we can provide for deletion/audit (by Aug 6).
- Schedule a legal/infosec sync if Medisafe wants deeper evidence review (suggest Aug 6 or 7).

Attachments: Redwood-DataRetention-FAQ.pdf (attached)

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0114

From: Ava Hart <ava.hart@medisafe.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
Cc: privacy@medisafe.io
Date: 2027-08-04T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope and legal path for ephemeral data handling (short retention pilot)

Thanks, Tessa — appreciated the recap. Attaching our internal PII matrix (Medisafe_PII_Matrix.xlsx) — shows which fields must be treated as sensitive/non-persistent for demos vs production. A few clarifications from Legal/InfoSec before we move to SOW: 

1) 0-retention for PII:
- Legal asks whether Redwood can guarantee that certain fields are never written to persistent logs or backups (i.e., true zero persistence). If not feasible, what exact mitigations exist (end-to-end encryption, immediate purge workflow, ephemeral memory only)?

2) Deletion proof / evidence:
- For the pilot they want a reproducible deletion procedure and logs showing deletion completion. Will Redwood provide deletion confirmation events and a retention report? Format has to be something Legal can digest (CSV/JSON) and include timestamps and actor IDs.

3) Customer-managed keys:
- For production we require CMK via KMS/HSM. For pilot, will Redwood accept a temporary CMK (or provide attestations) or is platform-only encryption acceptable?

4) Residency & isolation:
- Confirm pilot environment will be limited to us-east-1 and that there won't be cross-region backups.

5) Minimal logs:
- For the demo we propose an even shorter retention than 24h if possible — 4–6 hours for full request traces, with non-identifiable metrics tracked longer. Is sub-24h window supported programmatically?

If you can provide a short written response to those five bullets and a sample deletion certificate format, Legal will be in a better position to sign off on a pilot SOW. We are also open to a quick legal call next week — copying our privacy alias.

Thanks —
Ava Hart
Head of Privacy, Medisafe IO
ava.hart@medisafe.io

Attachment: Medisafe_PII_Matrix.xlsx

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Ava Hart <ava.hart@medisafe.io>, privacy@medisafe.io
Date: 2027-08-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot scope and legal path for ephemeral data handling — proposed negotiation approach

(Internal) Quick plan to respond to Medisafe's five bullets — proposal below so Ben/Marissa can align on what we offer and what requires Legal escalation.

Summary & recommended offer:
- 0-retention for PII fields: we cannot guarantee absolute platform-level 0-retention without code changes, but we can provide a configuration that ensures PII is never persisted to long-term logs and is only kept in ephemeral KV/cache while the session is active. For strict 0-retention we propose: field-level on-the-fly redaction + ephemeral session only, with a deletion confirmation event.

- Deletion proof: Redwood can produce deletion confirmation records (signed event entries) showing timestamp, resource id, and actor (system). We currently export audit events as JSON lines; propose to provide a CSV sample that Legal can consume. This will need a short-run by Infra engineers; request a 48–72 hour lead to produce the sample.

- CMK/KMS: Pilot options — (1) platform-managed keys (fastest), (2) temporary customer-managed key (we can accept a short-lived CMK token for pilot), (3) full KMS/HSM integration for production only. For Medisafe, suggest temporary CMK for the pilot to satisfy Legal without full integration effort.

- Residency: Confirmed — pilot environment can be restricted to us-east-1 with explicit non-replication. We'll include this in the SOW.

- Sub-24h retention: We can support sub-24h TTLs programmatically (down to 1 hour) for KV/cache and request traces retained in minimal form. However, our audit and metrics systems aggregate by day by default — to provide short-window raw traces we will need to enable a short-term trace export (engineering task, ~2–3 business days).

Action items I suggest we take now: 
- Ben: produce a draft one-page SOW with the pilot options and price impact (24h vs 4–6h vs 0-retention with additional engineering), include an SLA-lite clause for pilot.
- Marissa: flag any contract/term language we should avoid in SOW re: "guarantee" vs "reasonable commercial efforts". Also confirm whether the deletion certificate format below is acceptable to Legal (I will draft an example).
- Tessa: I'll draft the deletion certificate example and a short technical appendix mapping our knobs to Medisafe_PII_Matrix fields.

Suggested timeline: SOW + deletion cert draft by Aug 6 -> Legal sync (Medisafe + Redwood) Aug 6 or 7 -> pilot kickoff the following week pending sign-off.

Thoughts?

Tessa
